# Patch inventory

Every patch Astro applies, in the order its `series` file declares, with
what it touches and what is meant to happen to it.

Dispositions live in `patch-dispositions.json` and are joined in strictly:
a patch with no disposition, or a disposition for a patch that no longer
exists, fails generation. This inventory therefore cannot silently rot.

No published rmp-serde satisfies both adblock 0.9.8's ^0.15 and a current rmp, and constraining rmp below 0.8.11 would pin the decoder at 0.8.10 and falsify 066's [crate.rmp] README input declaration. | 66 | `070-theme-color-picker-astro-presets.patch` | `chrome/browser/ui/BUILD.gn`<br>`chrome/browser/ui/webui/cr_components/theme_color_picker/theme_color_picker_handler.cc` | 6 | **replace** | Rebuilds ThemeColorPickerHandler around Astro's Bloom presets: GetChromeColors serves the presets this build OFFERS (astro::IsColorPresetOffered over the generated gate table, 16 of Bloom's 18) instead of Chromium's thirteen GM3 colours, SetSeedColor stores the clicked one through AstroThemeService::SetColorPreset, and UpdateTheme reports the active preset so the check mark follows astro.theme.preset however it was changed. Before it the picker wrote browser.theme.user_color2, which lands in ColorProviderKey::user_color and so never reached the Astro mixer -- the panel recoloured itself and the sys palette while the toolbar, tabs and menus stayed on the stored preset. The GM3 seed is still written, set to the preset's own Bloom primary, because the mixer sets no ui::kColorSys* token and everything derived from those would otherwise keep an unrelated palette. Bloom gates faircoin and oxy to the accounts whose brands they are and sells mono with a subscription; Astro offers the ungated ones plus its own default, oxy, and upstream's Grey swatch writes the ungated gray rather than the premium mono. The handler is shared, so the Customize Astro side panel, astro://settings' appearance picker and chrome://profile-customization all move together. The hue slider behind the custom-colour circle is refused and logged: Astro has presets and no arbitrary seed, and deciding what a custom colour means here belongs to #24. |
| 67 | `071-whats-new-webui-takeover.patch` | `chrome/browser/ui/webui/chrome_web_ui_configs.cc` | 3 | **replace** | Swaps upstream's WhatsNewUIConfig for Astro's AstroWhatsNewUIConfig, so astro://whats-new is served by the Astro application. A swap rather than an addition because AddWebUIConfigImpl CHECKs on a duplicate origin. It also makes the host resolve at all: upstream's config declines every navigation outside a Google-branded build, since IsWebUIEnabled returns whats_new::IsEnabled() and that reads a feature flag disabled by default -- measured, the address answered net::ERR_INVALID_URL. |
| 68 | `072-webui-csp-style-src-attr.patch` | `content/browser/webui/url_data_manager_backend.cc` | 1 | **replace** | Adds StyleSrcAttr to the hard-coded list of CSP directives url_data_manager_backend.cc assembles a WebUI response header from. OverrideContentSecurityPolicy accepts and stores the directive without it, so before this patch all five Astro pages declared `style-src-attr 'none';` and none of them had it: a provoked setAttribute('style', ...) applied on every page, while the browser's own report of a refused remote stylesheet named `style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'` as the policy in force. Byte-identical for any source that does not set the directive, since the default for it is the empty string. |
| 69 | `073-management-webui-takeover.patch` | `chrome/browser/ui/webui/chrome_web_ui_configs.cc` | 2 | **replace** | Swaps upstream's ManagementUIConfig for astro::AstroManagementUIConfig, so astro://management is served by the Astro application. A swap rather than an addition because AddWebUIConfigImpl CHECKs on a duplicate origin. Safe to swap because ManagementUI is named in zero files under chrome/browser/ui/views/, where GetAs<T>() returning nullptr on a type mismatch is dereferenced unchecked -- ReadingListUI is named in three and IntroUI in two, which is why neither is taken this way. The Astro controller adopts upstream's ManagementUIHandler wholesale, so the page's facts stay the browser's; what goes is a support.google.com link the browser embedded as markup in its own explanation of who controls it, the product being named Chromium, and a banner opening the Google Admin console with a campaign parameter. |

### Overlapping patches (93)

Files touched by more than one patch. Touching one file is not proof
two patches conflict, but every real conflict is in this set, so it is
a candidate list rather than a verdict.
